Fewer public entry points and unified ggplot2 graphics in 0.3.0

Source: R/help_api_migration_030.R
mfrmr_api_migration_030.Rd

Related operations now use arguments or standard S3 methods, and all plot() methods render and return ggplot2 objects directly. Because 28 overlapping entry points are no longer exported and plot() returns a ggplot object rather than mfrm_plot_data / base graphics, the target release is versioned as 0.3.0 under semantic versioning: update old scripts before installing this development version. Existing saved result classes retain their summary(), plot(), plot_data(), and as_ggplot() methods.

Replacements

Former entryCurrent call

facets_term_crosswalk()facets_guide("terms")
facets_visual_contract()facets_guide("visuals")
facets_feature_coverage(status)facets_guide("coverage", status = status)

mfrmRFacets(...)run_mfrm_facets(...)

freeze_mfrm_calibration(x)update(x, status = "frozen")

mfrmr_interval_guide(scope)mfrmr_output_guide("intervals", scope)

Keep named clustering controls such as linkage or seed. They apply only to the chosen method; unsupported controls fail instead of being ignored. The default is still PAM, including the original third and fourth positional arguments weights and missing. For PCA k-means input, set scaling, weights and missingness when constructing the PCA, as before.

For calibration transitions, rename a named calibration argument to object and the state-specific timestamp argument to at_utc. Transitions still return a new object; they do not edit the input or a saved file. A draft must be validated before it can be frozen. Superseding or retiring requires a distinct record_id; update() cannot thaw or rewrite a frozen calibration. review_mfrm_calibration() remains a non-mutating review.

For file normalization, rename named population_file, item_file and case_file to conquest_population, conquest_item_estimates and conquest_case_eap. Keep delimiter and column-mapping controls by name. Raw ConQuest exports remain a separate bundle-dependent contract, handled by normalize_conquest_overlap_exports(). Do not feed them to the extracted table route. The common quadrature-sensitivity entry also accepts RSM/PCM; code that specifically requires GPCM should check the model it supplies.

Imputation pooling, comparison of partitions, model fitting and result extraction remain distinct operations. Similar names do not imply the same statistical target.

Unified ggplot2 return contract

All plot() S3 methods now render with ggplot2 (ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0) in Imports) and invisibly return a ggplot object (inherits(p, "ggplot")). Setting draw = FALSE constructs and returns the ggplot object without printing it or opening a graphics device.

Update scripts that previously indexed p$data$... on a returned mfrm_plot_data list to call plot_data() (plot_data(p) for the full payload list, plot_data(p, component = ...) for a named table/matrix, or plot_data(p, "notes") for descriptions and cautions) and plot_data_components() to inspect available components.

Saved plot payloads from 0.2.x (mfrm_plot_data, mfrm_design_evaluation_plot_data, and mfrm_signal_detection_plot_data) remain compatible with both plot_data() and as_ggplot(), and calling as_ggplot(p) on a 0.3.0 ggplot return value is idempotent. Two-continuous-variable scatterplots (including the new plot(dif, type = "scatter") route after analyze_dff(), model comparisons, fit pathway, fair average, bias, PCA scores, and recovery scatterplots) add aligned X/Y marginal histograms via marginal = c("auto", "histogram", "none"). These changes do not add support for previously unsupported models or uncertainty calculations.

Structured fit_mfrm() signature and shared spec

fit_mfrm() now exposes a focused 19-argument signature (data, 15 common model/design arguments, spec = NULL, control = list(), and ...) that partitions all 55 canonical arguments into data (1), spec (33 model, scale, identification, anchor, interaction, and population keys), and control (21 quadrature, optimizer, shrinkage, JML correction, and runtime keys).

  • Full-name flat arguments remain supported: Supply the complete names of the 55 canonical arguments directly to fit_mfrm() or in the named list passed to do.call(fit_mfrm, ...). Their defaults and statistical meaning are unchanged. Only the first four positional arguments (data, person, facets, score) retain their old positions; name all later arguments. Abbreviations for arguments now routed through ... are rejected. For example, replace quad_point = 15 with quad_points = 15 or control = list(quad_points = 15).

  • Shared 4-entrypoint spec: One named spec = list(...) can be passed unchanged to describe_mfrm_data(), review_mfrm_anchors(), fit_mfrm(), and export_mfrm_model() (data = ..., spec = spec) within each function's supported scope. A valid native fit specification is not necessarily exportable: ordinary RSM/PCM export requires a fixed standard-normal population; estimated intercept-only normal populations are supported only for one-family GPCM in Stan. Explicit top-level arguments override entries in spec; misplaced or duplicated keys fail with actionable guidance.

  • Technical reference page: Specialist equations, identification rules, JML polish-ladder details, and return-object provenance now live in fit_mfrm_technical_details (linked from fit_mfrm()). Use mfrmr_output_guide("core_workflow") for the five-step onboarding map.

For an existing rating table ratings with scores 1–4, these calls show how to migrate partial names and positional arguments. Run only the current form:

# Old: fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
#               1, 4, method = "MML", model = "RSM", quad_point = 15)
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  ratings, person = "Person", facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score", rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4,
  method = "MML", model = "RSM",
  control = list(quad_points = 15)
)

The example preserves the old default model constraints. Migration does not establish that those constraints are suitable for a particular assessment; review the population and location assumptions in fit_mfrm().
